name: Rachel Reeves
role: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer (2024-2026); Labour MP for Leeds West and Pudsey
summary: Labour economist and Chancellor who pairs fiscal rules and growth-first, pro-businesspolicy with NHS funding, taxes on the wealthy and defence and nuclear expansion.

notFound.work: Her books Alice in Westminster (2017) and Women of Westminster (2019)

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: As Chancellor she raised defence spending to 2.6% of GDP by 2027, the biggest rise since the cold war.

abortion-legal.rationale: She voted to decriminalise abortion in Northern Ireland and for the 2021 regulations providing services there.

assisted-dying.rationale: She voted for the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill at second reading and third reading, and again in 2026.

decide-locally.rationale: She said local transport decisions are better made locally and that the Government is giving mayors the powers and funding to make them.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: As Chancellor she changed the rules to ease North Sea tie-backs but also taxed windfall oil and gas profits and invested in renewables.

expand-nuclear.rationale: She voted for financing new nuclear plants and as Chancellor funded Sizewell C and small modular reactors.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: She voted to renew the Trident nuclear deterrent in 2016.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: She voted to renew Trident in 2016.

local-veto-new-housing.rationale: She casts those who block housing as the opposition and says the Government backs the builders, praising the planning overhaul.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: She voted against the Strikes (Minimum Service Levels) Bill at second reading.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: She voted against the 2021 aid cut in opposition, but as Chancellor cut the aid budget to pay for defence.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: She voted for the New Clause extending same-sex marriage to Northern Ireland.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: In 2016 she asked in the Commons whether the Government should do much more to crack down on tax havens.

social-market-economy.rationale: She describes growth as built by risk-taking firms the state should partner with, and a welfare system that protects those who cannot work.

state-directs-investment.rationale: She announced a steel strategy and the nationalisation of the Scunthorpe steelworks as industrial support for a strategic sector.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Her budgets abolished the non-dom regime and added VAT on private schools, higher capital gains tax and levies on private jets, raising about £30 billion from richer taxpayers.

unions-good.rationale: She voted for the regulations giving unions workplace access and time off for union duties.

universal-healthcare.rationale: As Chancellor she funded the NHS with about £29 billion a year more from her tax changes.

work-for-welfare.rationale: She set out Labour's compulsory jobs guarantee in 2015: long-term unemployed people would have to take a guaranteed job.
